chief_complaint: bulge in the groin and pain when coughing
hpi_details: 45F presents with a reducible bulge in her right groin that becomes prominent when coughing or standing. It causes mild aching pain at the end of the day.

core_concepts: Can be direct or indirect; both present as a groin bulge.
common_misconceptions: Thinking only men get inguinal hernias.
dangerous_errors: Missing signs of incarceration (irreducible, severely painful, overlying skin changes).
management_principles: Elective surgical repair for symptomatic reducible hernias.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: SAGES & ACS Evidence-Based Surgical Practice Guidelines

reference_soap.subjective: 45F with a reducible right groin bulge and mild discomfort.
reference_soap.objective: Right groin bulge present on standing/coughing, easily reducible. No overlying skin erythema.
reference_soap.assessment: Symptomatic reducible groin hernia; in a woman, distinguish inguinal from femoral hernia because femoral hernias carry a higher incarceration/strangulation risk.
reference_soap.plan: Refer to general surgery for timely elective repair and assess for a femoral hernia. Provide urgent return precautions for irreducibility, increasing pain, vomiting, abdominal distension, or skin changes.

learning_objectives: Identify symptomatic but uncomplicated inguinal hernias for elective repair.

teaching.one_liner: Reducible groin bulge exacerbated by increased intra-abdominal pressure, typical of an uncomplicated inguinal hernia.

must_ask.say: Does the bulge go away when you lie down or push on it?
Does the bulge get bigger or more noticeable when you cough, strain, or stand for a long time?
Is the bulge painful or tender to touch?
Has the bulge ever become stuck and not go back in, or turned red, hot, or very painful?
How long have you noticed the bulge, and has it changed in size?

history.answer: Hello doctor, I noticed a bulge in my right groin a few weeks ago, and it aches whenever I cough or stand for a long time.
I first noticed it about three weeks ago while lifting a heavy dresser at work.
It is in my right groin, just above the crease where my thigh meets my lower belly, and it does not go down into my labia.
It bulges out more when I stand on my feet all day or cough, and it goes flat when I lie down.
When I lie flat and gently press it with my fingers, it slips right back inside easily and has never stayed stuck.
It started roughly the size of a grape and has gradually grown to the size of a small walnut when I stand up.
It causes a dull, aching soreness toward the end of my work shift, but I have not had any sudden or severe sharp pain.
No, I have not had any belly ache, nausea, vomiting, or abdominal bloating.
My bowel movements are regular every day, and I am passing gas normally without any blockage.
No, the skin over the lump looks completely normal with no redness, bruising, or heat.
No, it does not throb or beat like a heartbeat at all.
No, I do not have any cuts, wounds, or sores on my legs, feet, or genital area.
No, I have had no fever, chills, or sweating episodes.
No, my weight has been stable, I have no night sweats, and I have not felt swollen glands anywhere else.
I cough only when I clear my throat from dust, not chronically, and I do not strain when urinating.
No, I do not suffer from constipation and I do not strain when having a bowel movement.
Yes, I work full-time as a professional mover, so I lift heavy boxes and furniture every single day.
I suspect I might have developed a hernia from all the heavy lifting I do at work.
I read online that a hernia can get pinched and cut off blood flow, so I am very worried about strangulation.
I want to have a surgical evaluation to see if I need an operation to repair it before it gets worse.
I do not have any chronic medical illnesses like high blood pressure or diabetes.
I have never had any surgeries on my abdomen or groin, and I have never been hospitalized except for childbirth.
I am not taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter painkillers, or herbal supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to medicines, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any nicotine products.
I drink one glass of wine occasionally on special occasions, but nothing regular.
I work as a residential mover and live with my husband and teenage daughter in a house.
There is no family history of hernias, connective tissue disorders, or abdominal diseases.
My last period started two weeks ago, and my menstrual cycles are always regular every twenty-eight days.
My husband had a vasectomy years ago, so there is no possibility that I am pregnant.
I have one child whom I delivered vaginally fifteen years ago without any complications.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 120/78 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.7 degrees Celsius, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert, oriented, and comfortable female in no acute distress.
Abdomen is flat and symmetrical with no surgical scars, distension, or visible peristalsis.
Normal active bowel sounds heard across all four quadrants with no vascular bruits.
Abdomen is soft, non-tender throughout, and non-distended without guarding or rebound tenderness.

A 3 cm soft bulge appears in the right groin above the inguinal crease on standing and coughing, easily reducible with gentle pressure, with mild tenderness on palpation and no overlying skin erythema.
Normal female external genitalia with no extension of the bulge into the labia majora and no palpable lymphadenopathy.
Femoral pulses are brisk and symmetric bilaterally with no expansile pulsation or bruit over the bulge.
